SMTO-HTTP-0063 — This web request uses an action type SMTO doesn't allow

GUID: 31d0b094-2ce6-46e2-a01b-ba6789197e21
Slug: http-method-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Every web request has an action type, such as GET to read or POST to send. This one was misspelled, too long, or one SMTO blocks (CONNECT or TRACE), so SMTO didn't send it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the service's documentation for the action it expects, for example GET to read data or POST to create something, and tell the Agent to use exactly that. SMTO only sends standard action types it can recognize.
  2. If you were testing a saved connection in Parameter Store, set Test method to GET, HEAD or OPTIONS and select Save. Connection tests only read from the service, so they allow just these three actions.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • If the service truly needs CONNECT or TRACE, SMTO can't make that request. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO to find another approach.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • normalize_method rejected the request method: it is not a valid HTTP token of at most 16 characters, or it is CONNECT or TRACE, which are intentionally unsupported.

What this means

  • The method is not a string token of at most 16 characters, or it is CONNECT or TRACE, which are explicitly rejected. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The method is not a string token of at most 16 characters, or it is CONNECT or TRACE, which are explicitly rejected.

How to diagnose it

  • Check token syntax and the explicit CONNECT/TRACE exclusion; do not guess support solely from familiar method names.

How to fix it

  • Use a valid method token of 16 characters or fewer, such as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. CONNECT and TRACE are rejected by design. A saved connection's test_request method must be GET, HEAD or OPTIONS.
  • Use a supported method; CONNECT and TRACE are intentionally unsupported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid supported method token passes admission.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
